Minutes before he was set to run his very first marathon, Piotr got the urge to urinate. After a year of training, he refused to miss the momentous moment because of biology. He had two choices: He could either run the 26.2 miles and pause occasionally to use the bathroom, or he could piss his pants.

He chose the latter.

Piotr went without a single bathroom break during the London Marathon in April in an effort to fight pee-shaming and to take a stand for all people around the globe who don't have access to port-o-potties or who have to "hide [their urine] away like it doesn’t exist."

He wrote about his experience in a Medium blog last month:

As I ran, I thought to myself about how women and men have both been effectively socialized to pretend urine doesn’t exist. By establishing a norm of pee-shaming, [hygiene-preferring] societies effectively prevent the ability to bond over an experience that 100% of us in the human population share several times a day. By making it "informal" or "unprofessional" to speak about, we don’t have the appropriate language to openly discuss our personal bodily functions in the workplace, and we don’t acknowledge that since they are universal, that means they should be displayed openly and shared with those around us. Because it is all kept quiet, people are socialized not to openly discuss and show the effects of their own bodily waste, since no one can see it happening. And if you can’t see it, it’s probably “not a big deal.” Why is this an important issue? Because THIS is happening, right now, yesterday, the day before yesterday, every day since the birth of our species and even before we evolved.

Piotr told Cosmopolitan he thinks the social constructs around urine are based on civility and hygiene.

I have this vision that if we didn't have a society with any standards of hygiene or common human decency, rules would be written into the workplace, rules would be written into the social fabric which would enable people to openly relieve themselves and urinate on everything - including each other," he said.

Two of the most important people in Piotr's life -- his mother and father -- were on the sidelines the day he ran the marathon. He was unsure how they would react to his statement, but when he reached them at the nine-mile mark, they only cared about hugging him and taking photos.

"When push comes to shove, all this cleaning that we do, all this shame that we feel, it doesn't matter," he told Cosmo. "They were my family, and they urinate too. On a spiritual level, that's amazing. That connects men and women in a very amazing way. Instead of men or women being grossed out by their own bodies, we should move away from that."

Piotr said he wanted to use the marathon to send a message to the world.

"If there's one way to transcend oppression, it's to run a marathon any way you want," he wrote on his personal website. "Where the distinction between human and animal is irrelevant, and we can re-write the rules as we choose."

I'm new to all of this.

Maybe you Googled "diapers" for the first time and by some measure of luck landed here. Maybe someone linked you here, maybe you were on the ABDL subreddit and realized you have to be 18 to hang out there. Whatever, you're here, and all you know is that for some long period of time, you've felt an inexplicable desire for diapers or babyish things. You might feel ashamed or embarrassed, or like you're the only person in the world who has these desires.

Well, guess what. You're not the only person! (If you didn't figure that out by the fact that you're reading this.) We have a bunch of names for it; the long scientific name is "paraphilic infantilism." People who have paraphilic infantilism are called adult babies, or ABs. There's a parallel sexual fetish for diapers; people who have that are called diaper lovers or DLs. Often, since there is a strong overlap, the whole group is referred to as "AB/DLs." By extension, a teenager with paraphilic infantilism might be called a teen baby/diaper love, or TB/DL.

Often times, people will bounce between being an AB/TB and DL. Teens tend to be more on the DL side - hormones and all that. As I've gotten older, I've found that my AB/little side has come out. Many of you will find the same to be true, while others will be more in touch with your cute little side and discover the DL aspects as you get older. Everyone experiences this a different way. That's perfectly okay.

What should I talk about?

Start by saying "hi". Introduce yourself and tell us who you are. The whole you, not just the diapers! Part of what helped me to be comfortable in my own skin is knowing that other normal kids were out there with this weird little interest. You might find a diapered friend who's into the same sport, instrument or craft as you.

From there, ask questions. There's a good chance that you're still new to this and have questions. No two parents are the same, and so, no two of your home lives are the same.

When you get your first pack of diapers, brag about it here. Seriously. It doesn't matter that there are a million other "first diapers" posts. It's an important moment, and it deserves a celebration!

Dealing with disposal, avoiding getting caught, controlling the damage after getting caught, figuring out deliveries and online payment, all of these are things you might need to know about. We're here for you - after all, being a TB/DL, at home, with parents and siblings around, is a whole lot harder than being an adult with your own digs.

Welcome, and have fun!

40 meg boot images to install Ubuntu and choose your desktop and software packages. A text installer that will install on older systems that won't support the graphical installer. I just used this to install Xubuntu and it works great.

Ok, there's some interest here so I'll post a few details. Since it's 40 meg it's quick to download. I made a CD but you can use a usb stick if your prefer. Several versions of Ubuntu are available from 12.04 LTS to 15.10 current latest. This is not a live CD, just an installer. The text installer starts and I just chose Install. There are other options but I was installing just xubuntu on the whole drive. Besides xubuntu (xfce) you can also choose other desktops like kde or media setups like mythbuntu. So this is an Ubuntu thing, not specifically Xubuntu even though I found it recommended on the Get Xubuntu web page.

On the same screen where you select your desktop you can also select software like Ubuntu Server, LAMP Server, Audio Studio, Video Studio, Photo Studio, and many other choices. There is also a select software choice at the bottom that I didn't try but my guess is it lets you pick packages.

It basically downloads everything while it's installing but that's pretty much unattended after you select your time zone and keyboard and user name. So the text installer is similar to the ubuntu graphical installer except I didn't see the auto login option or the third party media option.

I like that it lets me setup a minimal install using a text user interface on older systems. That's not what I'm doing now but I do intend to play with this in the future. I'm into taking systems that used to run XP or even older and making them work good with linux. This gives me an ubuntu option with the advantages of the ubuntu software library.
